answer: Keep Option A: 8 lessons of 40 minutes. This is the only choice that respects the binding decision (no 80-minute double periods) without inventing new lesson content. Splitting into about 14 lessons (Option B) needs new lessons to be written, so it cannot be done with wording edits. Because practice time is short, the one real edit below moves the Lesson 5 football-pitch check, which was already homework, into Lesson 6's warm-up so practice is not lost. Teachers can approve Option B later as a separate writing task.
alternative: Option B: split Lessons 1 and 3 to 8 into two 40-minute lessons each (about 14 lessons), with new lesson content written for each half.
knock_on: If Option B is chosen: all lessons need splitting, with new content, lesson numbers, DQB and model references, and the FE would need to cite the new lesson numbers. Otherwise none.
